mainTopic: For a נערה המאורסה, both the אב and the בעל must nullify her נדר, and the גמרא searches for the פסוק that teaches this.
overview: The משנה rules that for a נערה המאורסה, if only the father or only the husband nullifies her נדר, it stays in force, and even more so if one of them ratified it. The גמרא first asks why this is needed, since the משנה's opening line already said 'her father and her husband nullify.' It answers that we might have read that line as 'father OR husband.' Next it asks why the משנה mentions ratifying, when one person nullifying alone already fails. The answer is a special case: one nullified, the other ratified and then had a חכם cancel his ratification. Even then both must actually nullify together. The גמרא then asks for the תורה source that both the אב and the בעל annul a betrothed girl's vows. רבה brings the פסוק 'And if she will be to a man, and her vows are upon her.' The גמרא suggests this פסוק is about a married woman, answers that a married woman has her own פסוק, and then challenges that both פסוקים might be about a married woman, with the second teaching that a husband cannot annul earlier vows. The reply comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Father alone or husband alone cannot nullify
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if only the אב or only the בעל nullifies, the נדר is not nullified. It is certainly not nullified if one of them ratified it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father nullified and the husband did not, or the husband nullified and the father did not, the vow is not nullified. Needless to say, it is not nullified if one of them ratified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a rule about a betrothed girl's נדר: one person's הפרה alone does nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נערה המאורסה, the father and the husband share the power of הפרה. If only one of them acts, the נדר stays. If one of them actively confirms it (קיום), it obviously stays.

keyTerms.meaning: he ratified, actively confirmed the vow

steps.whatToRemember: For a נערה המאורסה, it takes BOTH the אב and the בעל to nullify.

phrases.english: If the father nullified and the husband did not nullify,
or the husband nullified and the father did not nullify —
it is not nullified.
And needless to say,
phrases.notes: Read it as 'needless to say it is not nullified.'

phrases.english: if one of them ratified it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One partner's הפרה alone is ineffective, and one partner's קיום certainly keeps the נדר in force.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the opening line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs this line, since the opening already said 'her father and her husband nullify her vows.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the same as the first clause: 'Her father and her husband nullify her vows'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for seeming to repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא of the משנה already said both father and husband nullify. That seems to already mean both are needed. So the new line looks redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: the first clause of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This is the same as the first clause:
Her father and her husband nullify her vows!
phrases.notes: This is the opening line of the same משנה, about a betrothed girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the משנה's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The line 'הפר האב ולא הפר הבעל אינו מופר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא already says both nullify, so this line seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The opening line could have meant 'father or husband'
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed because we might have read the רישא as 'either father or husband.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the משנה teaches 'either her father or her husband.' So it teaches us that both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה had to spell out that both are needed, because the opening line could be misread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אביה ובעלה' could be read as 'father OR husband,' meaning each one can nullify alone. The later line rules that reading out: one alone does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (a mistaken idea we could have had)
it teaches us (the point of the line)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
it teaches 'either her father or her husband,'
it teaches us otherwise (that both are needed).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא אוֹ אָבִיהָ אוֹ בַעְלָהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the line rules out a possible misreading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אביה ובעלה' could mean either one can nullify alone
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the אב and the בעל must nullify

steps.title: Why mention ratifying at all?
steps.stepSummary: If one person nullifying alone does nothing, it is obvious that one person ratifying keeps the נדר. So why does the משנה say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And needless to say if one of them ratified.' Why do I need it taught? Now, if one nullified without the other it is nothing, then one of them ratifying, why do I need it? Must it be taught?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the משנה and asks why it is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a הפרה by one alone has no effect. So when one of them actively ratifies, the נדר obviously stands. The line seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it to be taught?
now (if even the easier case is so)

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁקִּיֵּים אֶחָד מֵהֶן.
phrases.english: 'And needless to say if one of them ratified.'
Why do I need it to be taught?
Now, it was stated

phrases.aramaic: הֵפֵר זֶה בְּלֹא זֶה — וְלֹא כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: that if one nullified without the other, it is nothing;
if one of them ratified, why do I need it?
Is it necessary to teach this?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question on a different line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The line 'ואין צריך לומר שקיים אחד מהן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one person's nullifying alone fails, one person's ratifying obviously keeps the נדר, so the line is unnecessary.

steps.title: The case where a ratification was cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed for a special case. One nullified, the other ratified, and then the ratifier had his ratification cancelled. Even so, both must still nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed where one of them nullified and one ratified, and the one who ratified went back and asked a חכם to cancel his ratification. You might have said that what he set up, he has now uprooted. So it teaches us that both must nullify together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a special case that shows why the ratification line is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a ratification is cancelled, we might think the cancellation itself undoes the נדר. Then, together with the other one's הפרה, the נדר would be gone. The משנה teaches that cancelling a ratification is not a הפרה: both must actually nullify, together.

keyTerms.meaning: asked a חכם to cancel his ratification

steps.whatToRemember: Cancelling a קיום through a חכם does not count as a הפרה. Both the אב and the בעל must still nullify.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'cancelling the ratification' with 'nullifying the vow.' Undoing the קיום only removes the confirmation. It does not cancel the נדר itself.

phrases.english: It was necessary for it

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּהֵפֵר אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְקִיֵּים אֶחָד,
phrases.english: in a case where one of them nullified and one ratified,
and the one who ratified went back
and asked to have his ratification cancelled.
phrases.notes: He went to a חכם to have his ratification undone, the way one asks to undo a נדר.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
what he set up, he has now uprooted,
it teaches us
that they both must nullify together.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ כְּגוֹן דְּהֵפֵר אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְקִיֵּים אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the ratification line is needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a specific case where the line teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cancelling the ratification uproots it, so together with the other's הפרה the נדר is gone
steps.terutzMaskana: Both must actually nullify together; cancelling a ratification is not a הפרה
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that undoing a קיום and doing a הפרה are two different acts.

steps.title: Where does the rule for a betrothed girl come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a נערה המאורסה has her vows annulled by her אב and her בעל, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a betrothed young girl: her father and her husband annul her vows. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule about a betrothed girl and asks where the תורה teaches it. This question sets up the next move, where a source will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נערה המאורסה is still living in her father's house, so we might think her father alone should annul her vows. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that the husband is also involved.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl who is betrothed (has had אירוסין) but is not yet fully married
From where do we know this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: And a betrothed young girl,
her father and her husband annul her vows. From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the משנה's wording and opens a new question about the source of the opening rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that both the father and the husband annul a betrothed girl's vows.

steps.title: רבה's source: 'And if she will be to a man'
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings the פסוק 'And if she will be to a man, and her vows are upon her' as the source for the betrothed girl's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The פסוק says, 'And if she will be to a man, and her vows are upon her.' From here we learn that for a betrothed girl, her father and her husband annul her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by pointing to a פסוק about a girl who 'will be to a man' while her vows are still on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a girl who is becoming connected to a husband but is not yet in his house. רבה reads this as a נערה המאורסה. Since the husband is given a role here, he joins the father in annulling her vows.

phrases.english: Rabba said: The verse says:
"And if she will be to a man,
and her vows are upon her."
From here we learn about a betrothed young girl
that her father and her husband annul her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ואם היו תהיה לאיש ונדריה עליה' refers to a betrothed girl, so both her father and her husband annul her vows.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is about a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: perhaps this פסוק is talking about a fully married woman, not a betrothed girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that this פסוק is written about a married woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבה's reading. It says the words 'she will be to a man' could mean a fully married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is about a נשואה, then it does not teach anything about a betrothed girl. רבה's proof would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (instead) — offering another way to read something

phrases.english: Say that this verse
is written about a married woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's reading of the פסוק in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that 'ואם היו תהיה לאיש' refers to a betrothed girl.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'she will be to a man' could just as easily describe a married woman, so the פסוק proves nothing about a betrothed girl.

steps.title: A married woman has her own פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a married woman is taught in a different פסוק, 'And if she vowed in her husband's house.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want a פסוק for a married woman, there is another פסוק written: 'And if she vowed in her husband's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה. It says a married woman already has her own פסוק, so the first one must be about a betrothed girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק speaks of a woman already 'in her husband's house,' which is clearly a נשואה. So the earlier פסוק, about a girl who 'will be to a man,' is left to teach about a נערה המאורסה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is because of (if you need it for)
Her husband's house — the sign of a fully married woman

phrases.english: If it is for a married woman,
a different verse is written:
"And if she vowed in her husband's house."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם נְשׂוּאָה, קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and defends רבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-פסוק argument: one פסוק already covers the married woman, so the other must teach a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'ואם היו תהיה לאיש' might be about a married woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The married woman is taught by 'ואם בית אישה נדרה,' so the first פסוק refers to a betrothed girl.

steps.title: Maybe both פסוקים are about a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe both פסוקים are about a married woman, and the second one teaches that a husband cannot annul vows made before the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that both פסוקים are about a married woman! And if you ask why I need two פסוקים about a married woman, the answer is to teach that the husband cannot annul her earlier vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 9. It suggests both פסוקים speak about a married woman, and it even gives a reason why the תורה would need two of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 9 depended on the idea that two פסוקים cannot teach the same case. The גמרא now shows that the second פסוק could have its own job. By saying 'in her husband's house,' it teaches that a husband annuls only vows made after the marriage, not earlier ones. If so, there is still no source for the betrothed girl. The גמרא's reply comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (raising a possible objection ahead of time)
Earlier vows — ones she made before the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'לְמֵימַר שֶׁאֵין הַבַּעַל מֵיפֵר בְּקוֹדְמִין' are not the גמרא's final answer. They are part of the challenge itself. The גמרא is showing that the second פסוק could have its own purpose, which brings back the question about the betrothed girl.

phrases.english: Say that both are about a married woman?!
phrases.notes: 'Both' means both פסוקים: 'she will be to a man' and 'in her husband's house.'

phrases.english: And if you will say:
why do I need two verses about a married woman?
It is to say that the husband does not
annul earlier vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 by giving the second פסוק a separate purpose.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 9 that the second פסוק covers the married woman, which leaves the first פסוק for the betrothed girl.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both פסוקים could be about a married woman, since the second one has its own lesson: a husband cannot annul vows made before the marriage. So the first פסוק no longer has to be about a betrothed girl.
